The source names United States government work but not the agency. This record is not merged into a modern department or converted into a specific wartime agency.

affiliations.date_precision: The obituary places the Washington government work after business college and before her wartime transfer to Cairo; it supplies no agency or exact dates.
affiliations.research_notes: The unusual indexed surname and direct OSS-in-Cairo chronology support a probable identity. The source does not name the employing agency, job title, college, exact transition date or personnel-file identifier; the relationship is therefore qualified and requires Box 122 review.

affiliations.date_precision: Dartmouth's faculty notice dates his return as a sociology instructor to 1929, promotion to assistant professor to 1934 and full professorship to 1940. The sources state he was recruited by OSS in 1942 but do not give a formal leave or employment-end date.
affiliations.research_notes: Two Dartmouth sources independently connect the exact distinctive name, faculty role and 1942 OSS recruitment. They do not state the formal personnel action by which he left or took leave from Dartmouth, so immediacy is strongly date-bounded rather than explicit-immediate.

claims.claim_text: Nancy Andrews, identified in her obituary as Nancy Chopela/Tsopelas, is a probable match to the indexed Nancy Chopela.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The obituary preserves the unusual Chopela surname and states that she worked for OSS in Cairo during World War II.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact unusual surname and first name occur with direct OSS context, but one later obituary without a personnel-file identifier is not enough for a confirmed or high-confidence match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The obituary places Washington government work before wartime OSS work in Cairo but supplies no exact appointment or transfer dates.
claims.match_notes: Published as a probable match. The Tsopelas variant is retained as source context rather than a correction to the index spelling.

claims.claim_text: A qualified obituary chronology indicates that Nancy Chopela worked for an unspecified U.S. Government agency in Washington immediately before OSS work in Cairo.
claims.evidence_excerpt: she worked for the U.S. Government in Washington, DC. After World War II began, she was sent to Cairo Egypt
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The obituary describes Washington government work followed by a wartime transfer to Cairo, where Chopela worked for OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable identity based on the exact unusual first name and surname plus direct OSS context; no personnel-file identifier independently confirms the match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The narrative sequence supports probable immediacy, but no agency, job title, appointment date or transfer date is stated.
claims.match_notes: The broad U.S. Government description is preserved; the project does not invent an agency or treat business-college attendance as employment.

sources.locator_override: Washington government work followed by wartime OSS work in Cairo

claims.claim_text: The same qualified chronology identifies an unspecified U.S. Government agency as Nancy Chopela's last documented civilian affiliation before OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The obituary names no intervening civilian affiliation between her Washington government work and OSS work in Cairo.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable identity based on the uncommon name and OSS context; archival confirmation remains necessary.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable rather than certain: a narrative sequence is present, but exact dates and the employing agency are absent.
claims.match_notes: Government assignment is not collapsed into a named employer; no unsupported agency is supplied.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Michael E. Choukas is a high-confidence match to the Dartmouth sociology professor recruited by OSS in 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Dartmouth's faculty history supplies the exact name and OSS service; a separate oral history dates his OSS recruitment to 1942 and describes the same propaganda expertise.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact distinctive full name with middle initial, Dartmouth class and faculty history, wartime Washington move, OSS organization and propaganda specialty form a coherent match across two institutional sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: The oral history explicitly dates OSS recruitment to 1942, while the faculty notice dates his professorship to 1940 and OSS departure to 1945.
claims.match_notes: The personnel file remains unreviewed, so the identity is high-confidence rather than confirmed by a unique archival identifier.

claims.claim_text: Michael E. Choukas's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was his Dartmouth College sociology professorship.
claims.evidence_excerpt: he was—because of this he was recruited by the OSS in 1942
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Dartmouth records show Choukas on its sociology faculty from 1929, a full professor in 1940, and recruited by OSS in 1942 because of his propaganda expertise.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity supported by the exact distinctive name and matching institutional, professional and OSS details in two Dartmouth sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: The faculty and recruitment chronology is strongly date-bounded to Dartmouth immediately before the 1942 OSS recruitment; no intervening affiliation is reported.
claims.match_notes: The record does not invent a formal leave date or characterize his OSS status as military service.

claims.claim_text: Dartmouth College is Michael E. Choukas's last documented civilian employer before his OSS service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: returned to Dartmouth as an instructor in sociology in 1929
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Dartmouth's faculty account traces his employment from a 1929 instructorship through a 1940 full professorship and then directly to wartime OSS work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity based on the exact distinctive name and consistent Dartmouth-to-OSS chronology across two institutional sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded: Dartmouth employment is documented immediately before the 1942 OSS recruitment, with no intervening civilian employer in the reviewed sources.
claims.match_notes: Last civilian employer is modeled separately from immediate affiliation even though both point to Dartmouth in this case.

claims.claim_text: An institutional Korean history identifies an OSS India-Burma Theater sergeant named Stanley Choy; it is a probable match to the index entry.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Independence Hall of Korea entry names Stanley Choy as an OSS sergeant who interpreted an interrogation in New Delhi in 1945.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact English name and direct OSS context support a probable match, but the source supplies no middle name, private identifier or Box 122 linkage.
claims.temporal_assessment: The entry documents an OSS assignment in New Delhi in 1945 but gives no pre-OSS employer or recruitment chronology.
claims.match_notes: Published as a probable identity only. The Korean name form is retained as a search variant, not declared a correction to the index.
